assessment.rationale: Spans 149-150 establish that general-purpose servers are designed for worldwide hypertext systems and many contexts, but do not state they must support GET and POST.
assessment.provenance_note: General-purpose design intent stated; no conformance requirement for methods extracted.
limitations: No explicit method support requirement in general-purpose server description

excerpts.text: HTTP was created for the World Wide Web (WWW) architecture and has evolved over time to support the scalability needs of a worldwide hypertext system.

assessment.rationale: Span 114 states conformance includes semantics of protocol elements sent. Span 179 states servers MUST NOT assume same user agent on persistent connections; neither directly addresses GET/POST support as a requirement.
assessment.provenance_note: Conformance scope and connection handling stated; no GET/POST extraction.
limitations: No method support requirement extracted

excerpts.text: Conformance to HTTP includes both conformance to the particular messaging syntax of the protocol version in use and conformance to the semantics of protocol elements sent.
As a result, a server MUST NOT assume that two requests on the same connection are from the same user agent unless the connection is secured and specific to that agent.

assessment.rationale: Span 22 states Internet Standard status for the RFC, confirming it is a worldwide standard dated 2022, but does not enumerate required methods.
assessment.provenance_note: Internet Standard designation and 2022 date confirmed; method list not provided.
limitations: No method inventory in standard status paragraph

assessment.rationale: The specification identifies many specific server implementations (spiders, billboard screens, household appliances, etc.) but does not define a bounded set called 'general-purpose servers'.
assessment.provenance_note: The term 'general-purpose' describes the protocol's design intent, not a specific category of servers with compliance obligations.
limitations: No explicit definition of the server category in scope

assessment.rationale: Span 796 states 'Most HTTP communication consists of a retrieval request (GET) for a representation' but provides no assertion that POST is a required method for general-purpose servers.
assessment.provenance_note: Only GET is described as the primary communication pattern; no requirement for POST support is stated.
limitations: No mention of POST as a requirement for servers

excerpts.text: Most HTTP communication consists of a retrieval request (GET) for a representation of some resource identified by a URI.

assessment.synthesis_coverage: The cited spans establish that June 2022 IETF standardization and RFC publication occurred for HTTP, but do not themselves define method support requirements. They confirm the timeframe and global scope of the standard referenced in the claim.

excerpts.text: On 6 June 2022, IETF standardized HTTP/3 as RFC[9114](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9114)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTTP#cite_note-rfc9114-69).
In June 2022, RFC documents were published that deprecated many of the previous documents and introducing a few minor changes and a refactoring of HTTP semantics description into a separate document.
